child.title: orchestrating-issue-backlog: pre-score the Step 4 rubric with TypeSafe Scores, weights stay in the formula
child.body:
**What:** [Step 4](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/orchestrating-issue-backlog/SKILL.md#step-4-scoring-rubric) scores every issue on three dimensions with concrete 1–3 levels, then combines them with a formula the user may re-weight: `(Foundation × 2) + (Correctness × 2) + Scope`. The agent assigns each score by reading.

**Proposal:** an optional script that pre-scores the backlog. This is TypeSafe's [composite-scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) pattern: Jev scores the dimensions, and the weights stay in code.
- **Correctness Risk** and **Scope Clarity:** one **Score** each per issue, with the rubric's level descriptions as the levels, verbatim.
- **"Does this issue name a decision it leaves unresolved?"** One **Noul** per issue. This feeds the existing *decide-then-rescore* rule directly, so the decisions to raise at the approval gate surface before the table is presented.
- **Foundation Leverage** is relational, not a property of one issue. Ask one **Noul** per ordered pair: "Would resolving `issues[i]` unblock or simplify `issues[j]`?" Code then maps the count of confident pairs onto levels 1–3. Pairs grow as n²: for 40 issues that is 1,560 questions. Prefilter pairs in code (shared paths, labels, cross-references) and measure the request sizes against the 64k-per-request / 32k-per-question limits before choosing a batching scheme.

The table shows Jev's scores beside the agent's. A score with low confidence, or one that disagrees with the agent's, marks an issue to read in full.

**Bonus:** when the user re-weights the formula at the gate, the table recomputes without re-running inference, because the judgments haven't changed.

**Must not:** replace the HARD-GATE. The user still approves the scored table, and blast radius stays a sequencing input computed by code.

**Evaluation:** the approved tables in cohort design docs, and the re-scores recorded in process-log entries (e.g. the 14 → 16 move in the 2026-08-11 observo log), are the labels.

child.title: docs conventions: an advisory TypeSafe Choice per added sentence flags a present-tense claim about another repo, without the network gate the convention rejected
child.body:
**What:** [docs/CONVENTIONS.md § Claims about another repository](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/CONVENTIONS.md#claims-about-another-repository) bans stating another repo's current state in the present tense ("every cohort repo runs…"). A claim must be either **a shape without names** or **a dated observation** with the command that re-derives it, and **an event** needs neither form. The rule came from #322: a present-tense claim about `CannObserv/power-map`'s `scripts/pre-ship.sh` was cited as evidence two days after the file was deleted. The convention also says **"Do not gate this"**, because a test that queries GitHub for thirteen repos adds a network dependency to the suite. So today nothing catches a violation except a reviewer's eye.

**Proposal:** the gate the convention rejected would *verify* each claim against GitHub. Spotting the banned form is a different judgment, one that needs no GitHub call: is this sentence about another repo, and which of the convention's forms is it in? An optional, advisory script runs over the **added lines of a diff** in `*.md` files:
- **Code** splits the added prose into sentences, skipping fenced code and inline code spans.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per diff,** a **Choice** per sentence over {**shape without names**, **dated observation**, **event**, **present-tense claim about another repo's current state**, **not about another repo**}. Each option's criteria quote the convention's own definition and examples.
- **Output:** the sentences whose peak is *present-tense claim*, with the convention's two allowed rewrites linked.

**Where it runs:** beside `pre-ship.sh` or in reviewing-code's documentation pass, **never inside the pytest suite**. That keeps the convention's network-dependency reason intact.

**Must not:** block a commit. A flagged sentence is a prompt to choose a form; the author may decide it's an event.

**Why it matters:** the convention is right that verification can't be gated, but detection can be advisory, and a present-tense claim slips through review because it reads as a plain fact.

**Evaluation:** `git log -p` over `docs/` and `skills/**/*.md` finds sentences rewritten from present tense into an observation, which are positives (e.g. the #322 fix). The convention's own examples are fixed test cases.

child.title: process logs: TypeSafe Nouls spot a finding's second occurrence, the signal the promotion rule waits for
child.body:
**What:** three skills keep a per-run process log: [coordinating-epics](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/coordinating-epics/references/process-log.md), [orchestrating-issue-backlog](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/orchestrating-issue-backlog/references/process-log.md) and [patching-hosts](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/patching-hosts/references/process-log.md). Each promotes a recurring pattern into the skill and lists it under *Rules promoted into the skill* with the findings it came from. coordinating-epics states the rule as "a pattern that recurs in two runs, or that prevented damage once, is promoted." patching-hosts adds where a rule goes: a pattern that recurs on one environment goes into that environment's profile, and one that recurs across environments goes into the core. Spotting the recurrence is done by memory. A new run's findings have to be matched against every earlier entry's findings and every promoted rule, and as the logs grow, a second occurrence can go unnoticed.

**Proposal:** an optional script that runs when an entry is journaled. Code parses the new entry's findings, the promoted rules, and the earlier entries' unpromoted findings. Then one [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per new finding asks:
- a **Noul** per promoted rule: "Is `finding` another instance of `rules[j]`?" A high value means the finding should be cited under that rule, not re-promoted;
- a **Noul** per earlier unpromoted finding: "Do `finding` and `prior[k]` describe the same failure, even in different words or repos?" A high value means a **promotion candidate**: the second occurrence the rule is waiting for;
- a **Choice** over the skill's SKILL.md and reference headings (for patching-hosts, also its `environments/<id>.md` profiles), plus *none*: "Which section owns the step this finding is about?" The answer names where a promoted rule would land.

**Output:** for each finding, any existing-rule matches, promotion candidates with the earlier finding's run and number, and the owning section. All of it goes into the journaling agent's view.

**Must not:** promote anything. Promotion stays a judged edit to SKILL.md, made under the self-budget ratchet.

**Why it matters:** this rule is how a run's lessons reach the skill, and it depends on someone remembering that they've seen a pattern before. Across three skills, many runs and hundreds of numbered findings, that memory is the bottleneck. The section map also turns the logs into data: which sections produce the most lessons is a measured signal for which sections to revise.

**Evaluation:** the *Rules promoted into the skill* lists already record which findings were judged to be the same pattern (e.g. "From 2026-10-09 archiver (10, 17), 2026-10-13 status (18) …"). Those groupings are a ready-made labelled set for the pair Noul.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).

child.title: shipping-work: a TypeSafe Noul per issue requirement builds a requirements-vs-commits table for the Step 6 close gate
child.body:
**What:** every shipping-work variant has the same Step 6 HARD-GATE ([baseline](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/shipping-work/SKILL.md#step-6--close-github-issues)): "Re-read the issue body. Confirm each stated requirement is addressed in commits. If any requirement is missing: do NOT close." The check is a single act of reading, and nothing in what the user sees shows which requirements were matched to which commits.

**Proposal:** an optional script that runs before `close-issue.sh` and produces a requirements table:
- **Code extracts the requirements** from the issue body (checklist items, list items, paragraphs under a "Suggested fix" or "Acceptance" heading) and the evidence from the commit range: messages, changed paths, and the hunks of each changed file.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per issue,** with the requirements and the evidence in the state. It asks a **Noul** per requirement: "Do the changes in `commits` address `requirements[i]` as stated, not just touch the same area?"
- **Output:** a requirement / probability / closest-commit table. The agent shows it at the gate, and a weak row turns into the gate's existing question: descope or continue?

**Must not:** close anything, or count as the gate's verification. The HARD-GATE's wording is unchanged, and a high probability doesn't excuse re-reading the body.

**Why it matters:** an issue closed with a missing requirement is reopened by whoever runs into the gap, usually long after the context is gone. A table makes a requirement that got skimmed past visible at the one moment it is cheap to act on.

**Costs to measure first:**
- **Context limits:** diffs push against the 64k-per-request / 32k-per-question limits. Send hunks scoped to each requirement's paths, not the whole diff.
- **Four copies:** the four variants (`shipping-work`, `-php`, `-python-fastapi`, `-python-click`) are self-contained, so the script and its SKILL.md step land in each. Start in the baseline, measure, then copy.

**Evaluation:** in this repo, issues closed and later reopened, plus "descoped to #N" comments, give positives. Issues closed and never revisited give negatives.

- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).

child.title: reviewing-code: record each finding's tier and directive (the labelled set #437 needs)
child.body:
Split from #437 by the TypeSafe epic (#451). #437's Score per finding can't be measured until something records how findings were *judged*. Today only fixed findings leave a trace, as `CR N` commits. Stet and GH decisions disappear, and so does the tier each finding was given.

child.title: reviewing-code: a TypeSafe Score per finding as a calibration check on its severity tier
child.body:
**What:** Phase 3 sorts findings into 🔴 Bugs / 🟡 Issues to fix / 💭 Minor based on the reviewer's judgment alone. Nothing checks a tier call. Yet the tier steers the user's directives, especially a blanket `address the findings`, which answers every tier in one pass.

**Proposal:** after Phase 3.5 verification, an optional script reads each finding (the required `What:` / `Why it matters:` / `Suggested fix:` labels make that parse reliable) plus the diff hunk at its `file:line`, and sends one [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request with:
- a **Score** per finding on three levels, each describing a concrete situation (e.g. *produces wrong output, a crash, or data loss on an input the code can reach* / *a correctness or maintenance cost a user or later change will hit* / *style, naming, or an observation with no failure attached*);
- a **Noul** per finding: "Does `findings[i].why` name a concrete failure, meaning specific inputs or state leading to a specific wrong outcome?"

Where the Score's peak level differs from the reviewer's tier, or its [confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md) is low, the report marks the finding *tier contested*. The user then sees which calls to look at before giving directives. The reviewer's tier stays authoritative, and nothing is re-tiered automatically.

**Why it matters:** a finding that is really a bug, filed under 💭, can be stetted with the rest of its tier. A 🔴 with no failure scenario costs the user a careful read for nothing.

**Prerequisite:** directives aren't recorded durably today. Only fixed findings land, as `CR N` commits, and stet/GH decisions disappear. Recording each finding's tier and directive over a few rounds builds the labelled set; without it there is nothing to measure agreement against.

**Scope:** the variants (`-php`, `-python-fastapi`, `-python-click`) are self-contained, so start in the baseline and copy to the variants only once agreement has been measured.

**Constraints shared with the other TypeSafe proposals:**
- **Opt-in and advisory.** If `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is missing, the step skips and says so loudly, and the run goes on exactly as it does today. The opt-in knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md), which `test_skills_knob_inventory.py` requires.
- **Data leaves the machine.** This sends repo text to typesafe.ai. Today the only API call any skill script makes is `measure-context.sh --exact`'s token count, and that sends no text to be judged. Some cohort repos are private, so the opt-in is per repo, never cohort-wide.
- **Pin the model.** Use `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`. The alias moves when a new version ships, and thresholds tuned against one version don't carry to the next ([models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models.md#aliases)).
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does. A typed answer guarantees the shape of the answer, not that it is true.

child.title: curating-context: prove-no-loss --semantic, a TypeSafe Noul per base sentence asks whether a tightened section still states its rule
child.body:
**What:** `prove-no-loss.sh` enforces curating-context's iron law with two matchers ([its --help](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/curating-context/scripts/prove-no-loss.sh)). **Whole-line matching** sees a class-C tightening as 100% lost, because "a paragraph is one line." **`--claims`** checks atoms: backticked spans, `#NNN` references, link targets, bare URLs. Neither can see what a tightening most often drops, which is the *rule* between the atoms: a "never", a condition ("only when …"), an exception, or a reason. A rewrite can keep every atom and still change what the section tells an agent to do, and the verdict comes back `ok`.

**Proposal:** an optional, advisory `--semantic` pass for sections a run tightened:
- **Code pairs the sections:** each base section with its successor (same heading, or the one the run's `retarget` / `tighten` warrant names). It splits the base section into sentences and list items.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per section pair,** with `after_section` and the base sentences in the state. It asks a **Noul** per base sentence: "Does `after_section` still state what `base_sentences[i]` requires or forbids, including its conditions, exceptions and stated reason?" This is the [citation-check](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/citation_check.md) pattern: one claim checked against one source.
- **Output:** base sentences sorted by how unlikely they are to have survived, printed after the existing report.

**Must not:** move the verdict. `ok` / `failed` / `skipped`, exit 3, and both warrant files are unchanged. A low Noul means "re-read this sentence against the rewrite before you commit". It is not a loss, and never a pass either. The pass reports in its own section, so the `no_loss` and `claims_*` telemetry fields keep their meaning.

**Why it matters:** the iron law exists to stop content being dropped, and a tightening is the edit most likely to drop it without anyone seeing. Today the only check on a rewritten rule is that the agent re-read it.

**Evaluation:** cohort curation diffs that a later review corrected (a reverted or re-added clause) are positives, and tightenings that stood are negatives. Measure recall on the positives first: a miss here is worse than a false alarm.

**Related:** #435 classifies sections *before* the edit; this checks the edit *after*.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

child.title: curating-context: a TypeSafe Noul per index line checks it still describes its doc, and flags sibling lines that steal a topic's route
child.body:
**What:** an agent picks a reference doc by its **line in the policy file's index**, and curating-context has measured that being reachable through links doesn't make a doc findable ([cohort-patterns.md § Reachable is not routable](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/curating-context/references/cohort-patterns.md#reachable-is-not-routable)). A doc named nowhere in the policy file fell from 12/12 to 2/12 tasks reaching it, and a sibling line that named a topic better took every first hop. `docs_unindexed` counts docs with **no** line. Nothing checks whether an existing line still **describes** its doc after the doc grew, split, or absorbed a demotion. `check-counts.sh` bounds a line's *length*, not its accuracy.

**Proposal:** an optional, advisory pass in Phase 6.5:
- **Code** pairs each index line with its target doc's headings and opening paragraph, and lists the doc's `##` topics.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per policy file:**
  - a **Noul** per index line: "Would an agent reading only `index_line` expect to find what `doc.headings` covers, with no major topic missing and none claimed that isn't there?"
  - a **Noul** per (doc topic, index line naming a *different* doc): "Does `index_line` claim `topic` more directly than its own doc's line does?" This flags the sibling line that steals a route.
- **Output:** inaccurate lines and topic collisions, ranked, beside `check-seams.sh`'s report.

**Scope:** this checks whether a line *describes its doc accurately*. It does not *simulate routing*. Whether an agent actually finds the doc is a property of the agent's model, and the measurement in cohort-patterns.md should keep using the real agent. Jev standing in for it would measure a different model.

**Must not:** rewrite index lines, or count toward any gated telemetry field.

**Why it matters:** an inaccurate index line is a routing loss that every task pays and no current field records. The curation that caused it, a demotion that grew a doc, is exactly the run in which nobody re-reads that line.

**Evaluation:** index-line rewrites in cohort curation diffs (a line re-worded after its doc changed) are positives. The routing measurements above give a small set with known outcomes.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

child.title: curating-context: a TypeSafe Choice per section as a second reading of the Phase 3 class, recorded in the telemetry row
child.body:
**What:** Phase 3 gives each `##` section (and each subsection over ~5% of the file) one class, A/B/C/D, from [keep-cut-rubric.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/curating-context/references/keep-cut-rubric.md). That class is the most consequential call in a run: the skill itself says "compressing class B is wasted work, deleting class A is damage." Yet it is pure agent judgment, and the ledger records only the actions that followed (`demote:X`, `prune:Y`). Neither the class nor how close the call was is recorded.

**Proposal:** add an optional script that sends the policy file to [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) Jev as structured state (`sections[i].heading`, `.text`, `.tokens`). The request asks:
- one **Choice** per section over A/B/C/D, with each option's criteria taken from the rubric's class definitions, so the classes mean the same thing in the script as in the rubric;
- one **Noul** per section: "Does `sections[i].text` restate a default a capable coding agent already follows?" This is the one class-D clause a model can judge. *Duplicates another part of the surface* and *disproven* stay with Phase 2's scripts.

All of these go in one request ([speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md)). The script outputs JSON: per section, the class, its per-class probabilities, the confidence, and the Noul.

**How it's used:**
1. The agent's class stays authoritative. A section where Jev's class differs, or its confidence is low, gets a second look before Phase 4. It is never re-classed automatically.
2. A new telemetry field (e.g. `class_contested`, the number of contested sections, `null` when the step didn't run) lets the cohort roll-up see which classes are hard to call.

**Must not:** license a delete. The iron law's warrants (relocated, duplicated, disproven) are unchanged. A "D" from Jev with no warrant only means "look here".

**Why it matters:** the class is the one call in the run nobody checks. A probability distribution per section makes a contested call visible, before it turns into an edit, and after it, in the ledger.

**Evaluation:** past cohort runs give a labelled set. The ledger's action tags plus the curation diffs recover which sections were demoted, tightened or pruned. Measure agreement against those first. Cost [estimated]: at the listed $0.042/Mtok input price, a 6k-token policy file plus the questions costs well under a cent per run.

**Constraints shared with the other TypeSafe proposals:**
- **Opt-in and advisory.** If `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is missing, the step skips and says so loudly, and the run goes on exactly as it does today. The opt-in knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md), which `test_skills_knob_inventory.py` requires.
- **Data leaves the machine.** This sends repo text to typesafe.ai. Today the only API call any skill script makes is `measure-context.sh --exact`'s token count, and that sends no text to be judged. Some cohort repos are private, so the opt-in is per repo, never cohort-wide.
- **Pin the model.** Use `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`. The alias moves when a new version ships, and thresholds tuned against one version don't carry to the next ([models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models.md#aliases)).
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does. A typed answer guarantees the shape of the answer, not that it is true.

child.title: coordinating-epics: rank harvest candidates with a TypeSafe Noul per (paragraph, open child), so a note reaches a child it never names
child.body:
**What:** check-in §2, Harvest ([check-in.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/coordinating-epics/references/check-in.md#2-harvest)), reads the closing comment, the PR, and every comment since the hand-off. From them it routes contract diffs, `For #N:` notes, asides in prose, verification debt and corrections to the children they affect. An explicit `For #N:` heading names its target. The hard cases have no heading: a contract diff that should reach "every downstream child", or a later child's precondition mentioned in passing. Here the coordinator has to match a paragraph to a child it never names. Several log entries cite a note that didn't reach its child (archiver 19, 32; private-backlog 103, 110).

**Proposal:** add an optional script that produces a ranked list of harvest candidates:
- Code splits the harvest sources into paragraphs and fetches the open children's titles and bodies through `gh`.
- One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per source comment, with that comment's paragraphs and the open children in the state:
  - a **Noul** per (paragraph, child): "Does `paragraphs[i]` change a fact, contract, or step that `children[j].body` relies on?";
  - a **Choice** per paragraph over the harvest kinds in §2: contract diff, note for a later child, new state/code/message, verification debt, accepted limitation, correction to a claim, answer to a later child's step, or **none**.
- Output: (paragraph, child, kind, probability) rows sorted by the Noul, written to the coordinator's scratch, where it reads them beside `scan.json`.

**Must not:** write to GitHub. The coordinator still verifies each candidate and writes the "Changed since filed" comment, and the "coordinator never writes code" rule is unchanged. The script only reorders what the coordinator reads first.

**Why it matters:** a note that never reaches its child surfaces only when that child's implementer runs into it. The cost of a missed harvest is paid late and in someone else's thread.

**Evaluation:** the process-log issues (#428, #431 and their predecessors) record harvest misses together with the comment and child involved. Replaying those pairs gives a labelled set before the step is enabled anywhere. This is the [re-ranking](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md) pattern; a ranked list doesn't need a threshold to be useful.

child.title: coordinating-epics: a TypeSafe Choice per new item proposes its §3 slot, with a Noul per open child for duplicates
child.body:
**What:** at each check-in, `scan.sh` reports new items through three cursors (number watermark, updated-since, commit range). [check-in.md §3](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/coordinating-epics/references/check-in.md#3-re-scan-and-slot) then classifies each new item as **child**, **closed-in-fact**, **split**, **out of epic**, **duplicate**, or **park**, which is a closed set of six. The coordinator classifies each item by reading it, and a re-scan can return many items at once.

**Proposal:** an optional script that reads `scan.json` and proposes a slot for each item. One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per item, with the item (title, body, labels, state, linked PRs), the epic's goal and child lines, and the open children in the state:
- a **Choice** over the six outcomes, each option's criteria taken from §3's own definitions;
- a **Noul** per open child: "Does `item` describe the same work as `open_children[j]`?" The top match names the duplicate's survivor;
- a **Noul**: "Does `item` contain both work this epic covers and work it does not?" This is a signal for a split.

The output is the proposed slot, its probabilities and confidence, and the top duplicate candidate, written beside `scan.json`. Low confidence means the item gets a full read.

**Must not:** act. *closed-in-fact* still needs §1's evidence (merged, CI green on the final SHA, live), and all edits still go through `epic-edit.sh`, whose refusals are unchanged. A proposal only orders the coordinator's reading.

**Why it matters:** a duplicate or an out-of-epic item that gets slotted as a child costs a whole hand-off. The six outcomes are already defined, which is exactly the shape a Choice needs.

**Shares a loader with #436:** both read the same state (new comments or items, open children). Build them on one fetch.

**Evaluation:** where check-in log lines and epic edit history record how past items were slotted, they form the labelled set. Replay them before enabling the step.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435–#437):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

child.title: orchestrating-issue-backlog: at each batch boundary, a TypeSafe Noul per (claim, merged hunk) flags issue-body decay before workers launch
child.body:
**What:** orchestrating-issue-backlog carries a **runtime note on issue-body decay** ([SKILL.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/orchestrating-issue-backlog/SKILL.md)): "the backlog is N sequential mutations of what the bodies describe, so re-verify the specifics of any issue whose files an earlier batch touched (Worker step 5); the later the batch, the staler the body." reviewing-architecture records how bad this gets, measured: a 13-issue backlog carved from one review "carried a material error in **every** issue body by implementation time." One finding's branch-point table was 5 of 7 stale, because an earlier batch had changed a column type (process-log 2026-08-09 observo). The re-verify step relies on each worker noticing that its issue's files moved.

**Proposal:** an optional script the coordinator runs at each batch boundary, before workers launch:
- **Code** collects, for each issue in the next batch, the hunks merged since the issue was filed (or since its last "Changed since filed" comment) that touch the paths, symbols or tables its body cites. It also splits the body into claim sentences.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per issue,** a **Noul** per (claim, hunk): "Does `hunks[k]` make `claims[i]` untrue or out of date, for example a line, count, signature, column type or file it states?"
- **Output:** for each issue, the flagged claims with the hunk and merge commit that invalidates them. The worker's brief carries it, and the coordinator posts it as a "Changed since filed" comment, as coordinating-epics does.

**Must not:** edit issue bodies or reorder batches. The worker still re-verifies (step 5), and the script tells it where to look first.

**Why it matters:** the decay concentrates in the later batches, where the work is hardest. A worker that trusts a stale body re-does work or implements against a shape that's gone.

**Shares machinery with #436 and #439:** the same fetch of issues and comments, and the same paragraph and hunk splitting. Build it on that loader.

**Evaluation:** the Step 5 rescope comments and process-log entries record which bodies were stale and why. Replaying their batches gives labelled (claim, hunk) pairs.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

child.title: orchestrating-issue-backlog: pre-score the Step 4 rubric with TypeSafe Scores, weights stay in the formula
child.body:
**What:** [Step 4](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/orchestrating-issue-backlog/SKILL.md#step-4-scoring-rubric) scores every issue on three dimensions with concrete 1–3 levels, then combines them with a formula the user may re-weight: `(Foundation × 2) + (Correctness × 2) + Scope`. The agent assigns each score by reading.

**Proposal:** an optional script that pre-scores the backlog. This is TypeSafe's [composite-scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) pattern: Jev scores the dimensions, and the weights stay in code.
- **Correctness Risk** and **Scope Clarity:** one **Score** each per issue, with the rubric's level descriptions as the levels, verbatim.
- **"Does this issue name a decision it leaves unresolved?"** One **Noul** per issue. This feeds the existing *decide-then-rescore* rule directly, so the decisions to raise at the approval gate surface before the table is presented.
- **Foundation Leverage** is relational, not a property of one issue. Ask one **Noul** per ordered pair: "Would resolving `issues[i]` unblock or simplify `issues[j]`?" Code then maps the count of confident pairs onto levels 1–3. Pairs grow as n²: for 40 issues that is 1,560 questions. Prefilter pairs in code (shared paths, labels, cross-references) and measure the request sizes against the 64k-per-request / 32k-per-question limits before choosing a batching scheme.

The table shows Jev's scores beside the agent's. A score with low confidence, or one that disagrees with the agent's, marks an issue to read in full.

**Bonus:** when the user re-weights the formula at the gate, the table recomputes without re-running inference, because the judgments haven't changed.

**Must not:** replace the HARD-GATE. The user still approves the scored table, and blast radius stays a sequencing input computed by code.

**Evaluation:** the approved tables in cohort design docs, and the re-scores recorded in process-log entries (e.g. the 14 → 16 move in the 2026-08-11 observo log), are the labels.

- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).

child.title: docs conventions: an advisory TypeSafe Choice per added sentence flags a present-tense claim about another repo, without the network gate the convention rejected
child.body:
**What:** [docs/CONVENTIONS.md § Claims about another repository](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/CONVENTIONS.md#claims-about-another-repository) bans stating another repo's current state in the present tense ("every cohort repo runs…"). A claim must be either **a shape without names** or **a dated observation** with the command that re-derives it, and **an event** needs neither form. The rule came from #322: a present-tense claim about `CannObserv/power-map`'s `scripts/pre-ship.sh` was cited as evidence two days after the file was deleted. The convention also says **"Do not gate this"**, because a test that queries GitHub for thirteen repos adds a network dependency to the suite. So today nothing catches a violation except a reviewer's eye.

**Proposal:** the gate the convention rejected would *verify* each claim against GitHub. Spotting the banned form is a different judgment, one that needs no GitHub call: is this sentence about another repo, and which of the convention's forms is it in? An optional, advisory script runs over the **added lines of a diff** in `*.md` files:
- **Code** splits the added prose into sentences, skipping fenced code and inline code spans.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per diff,** a **Choice** per sentence over {**shape without names**, **dated observation**, **event**, **present-tense claim about another repo's current state**, **not about another repo**}. Each option's criteria quote the convention's own definition and examples.
- **Output:** the sentences whose peak is *present-tense claim*, with the convention's two allowed rewrites linked.

**Where it runs:** beside `pre-ship.sh` or in reviewing-code's documentation pass, **never inside the pytest suite**. That keeps the convention's network-dependency reason intact.

**Must not:** block a commit. A flagged sentence is a prompt to choose a form; the author may decide it's an event.

**Why it matters:** the convention is right that verification can't be gated, but detection can be advisory, and a present-tense claim slips through review because it reads as a plain fact.

**Evaluation:** `git log -p` over `docs/` and `skills/**/*.md` finds sentences rewritten from present tense into an observation, which are positives (e.g. the #322 fix). The convention's own examples are fixed test cases.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

child.title: process logs: TypeSafe Nouls spot a finding's second occurrence, the signal the promotion rule waits for
child.body:
**What:** three skills keep a per-run process log: [coordinating-epics](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/coordinating-epics/references/process-log.md), [orchestrating-issue-backlog](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/orchestrating-issue-backlog/references/process-log.md) and [patching-hosts](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/patching-hosts/references/process-log.md). Each promotes a recurring pattern into the skill and lists it under *Rules promoted into the skill* with the findings it came from. coordinating-epics states the rule as "a pattern that recurs in two runs, or that prevented damage once, is promoted." patching-hosts adds where a rule goes: a pattern that recurs on one environment goes into that environment's profile, and one that recurs across environments goes into the core. Spotting the recurrence is done by memory. A new run's findings have to be matched against every earlier entry's findings and every promoted rule, and as the logs grow, a second occurrence can go unnoticed.

**Proposal:** an optional script that runs when an entry is journaled. Code parses the new entry's findings, the promoted rules, and the earlier entries' unpromoted findings. Then one [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per new finding asks:
- a **Noul** per promoted rule: "Is `finding` another instance of `rules[j]`?" A high value means the finding should be cited under that rule, not re-promoted;
- a **Noul** per earlier unpromoted finding: "Do `finding` and `prior[k]` describe the same failure, even in different words or repos?" A high value means a **promotion candidate**: the second occurrence the rule is waiting for;
- a **Choice** over the skill's SKILL.md and reference headings (for patching-hosts, also its `environments/<id>.md` profiles), plus *none*: "Which section owns the step this finding is about?" The answer names where a promoted rule would land.

**Output:** for each finding, any existing-rule matches, promotion candidates with the earlier finding's run and number, and the owning section. All of it goes into the journaling agent's view.

**Must not:** promote anything. Promotion stays a judged edit to SKILL.md, made under the self-budget ratchet.

**Why it matters:** this rule is how a run's lessons reach the skill, and it depends on someone remembering that they've seen a pattern before. Across three skills, many runs and hundreds of numbered findings, that memory is the bottleneck. The section map also turns the logs into data: which sections produce the most lessons is a measured signal for which sections to revise.

**Evaluation:** the *Rules promoted into the skill* lists already record which findings were judged to be the same pattern (e.g. "From 2026-10-09 archiver (10, 17), 2026-10-13 status (18) …"). Those groupings are a ready-made labelled set for the pair Noul.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.

- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

child.title: shipping-work: a TypeSafe Noul per issue requirement builds a requirements-vs-commits table for the Step 6 close gate
child.body:
**What:** every shipping-work variant has the same Step 6 HARD-GATE ([baseline](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/shipping-work/SKILL.md#step-6--close-github-issues)): "Re-read the issue body. Confirm each stated requirement is addressed in commits. If any requirement is missing: do NOT close." The check is a single act of reading, and nothing in what the user sees shows which requirements were matched to which commits.

**Proposal:** an optional script that runs before `close-issue.sh` and produces a requirements table:
- **Code extracts the requirements** from the issue body (checklist items, list items, paragraphs under a "Suggested fix" or "Acceptance" heading) and the evidence from the commit range: messages, changed paths, and the hunks of each changed file.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per issue,** with the requirements and the evidence in the state. It asks a **Noul** per requirement: "Do the changes in `commits` address `requirements[i]` as stated, not just touch the same area?"
- **Output:** a requirement / probability / closest-commit table. The agent shows it at the gate, and a weak row turns into the gate's existing question: descope or continue?

**Must not:** close anything, or count as the gate's verification. The HARD-GATE's wording is unchanged, and a high probability doesn't excuse re-reading the body.

**Why it matters:** an issue closed with a missing requirement is reopened by whoever runs into the gap, usually long after the context is gone. A table makes a requirement that got skimmed past visible at the one moment it is cheap to act on.

**Costs to measure first:**
- **Context limits:** diffs push against the 64k-per-request / 32k-per-question limits. Send hunks scoped to each requirement's paths, not the whole diff.
- **Four copies:** the four variants (`shipping-work`, `-php`, `-python-fastapi`, `-python-click`) are self-contained, so the script and its SKILL.md step land in each. Start in the baseline, measure, then copy.

**Evaluation:** in this repo, issues closed and later reopened, plus "descoped to #N" comments, give positives. Issues closed and never revisited give negatives.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

child.title: reviewing-code: record each finding's tier and directive (the labelled set #437 needs)
child.body:
Split from #437 by the TypeSafe epic (#451). #437's Score per finding can't be measured until something records how findings were *judged*. Today only fixed findings leave a trace, as `CR N` commits. Stet and GH decisions disappear, and so does the tier each finding was given.

The location and format are this child's design call. child.title: reviewing-code: a TypeSafe Score per finding as a calibration check on its severity tier
child.body:
**What:** Phase 3 sorts findings into 🔴 Bugs / 🟡 Issues to fix / 💭 Minor based on the reviewer's judgment alone. Nothing checks a tier call. Yet the tier steers the user's directives, especially a blanket `address the findings`, which answers every tier in one pass.

**Proposal:** after Phase 3.5 verification, an optional script reads each finding (the required `What:` / `Why it matters:` / `Suggested fix:` labels make that parse reliable) plus the diff hunk at its `file:line`, and sends one [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request with:
- a **Score** per finding on three levels, each describing a concrete situation (e.g. *produces wrong output, a crash, or data loss on an input the code can reach* / *a correctness or maintenance cost a user or later change will hit* / *style, naming, or an observation with no failure attached*);
- a **Noul** per finding: "Does `findings[i].why` name a concrete failure, meaning specific inputs or state leading to a specific wrong outcome?"

Where the Score's peak level differs from the reviewer's tier, or its [confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md) is low, the report marks the finding *tier contested*. The user then sees which calls to look at before giving directives. The reviewer's tier stays authoritative, and nothing is re-tiered automatically.

**Why it matters:** a finding that is really a bug, filed under 💭, can be stetted with the rest of its tier. A 🔴 with no failure scenario costs the user a careful read for nothing.

**Prerequisite:** directives aren't recorded durably today. Only fixed findings land, as `CR N` commits, and stet/GH decisions disappear. Recording each finding's tier and directive over a few rounds builds the labelled set; without it there is nothing to measure agreement against.

**Scope:** the variants (`-php`, `-python-fastapi`, `-python-click`) are self-contained, so start in the baseline and copy to the variants only once agreement has been measured.

**Constraints shared with the other TypeSafe proposals:**
- **Opt-in and advisory.** If `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is missing, the step skips and says so loudly, and the run goes on exactly as it does today. The opt-in knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md), which `test_skills_knob_inventory.py` requires.
- **Data leaves the machine.** This sends repo text to typesafe.ai. Today the only API call any skill script makes is `measure-context.sh --exact`'s token count, and that sends no text to be judged. Some cohort repos are private, so the opt-in is per repo, never cohort-wide.
- **Pin the model.** Use `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`. The alias moves when a new version ships, and thresholds tuned against one version don't carry to the next ([models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models.md#aliases)).
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does. A typed answer guarantees the shape of the answer, not that it is true.

child.title: tightened-rules: count a rule delegated behind a link as kept — measured on #442's set before anything changes
child.body:
Follow-up to #442, filed by the epic #451 coordinator. **Decided 2026-10-23 by the operator:** keep `tightened-rules.sh`'s default threshold at 0.3, and **measure** whether a rule delegated behind a link should count as kept **before** changing anything. This issue is that measurement, plus the change if the numbers support it.

**What:** `tightened-rules.sh` (#442) sees only a tightened sentence's **successor section**. When a curation moves a rule into a reference doc and leaves a link, the pass reads it as dropped. That's the class-B *demote* the rubric prescribes. On #442's random slice that is **18 of 26 positives** ("survive only as a link to another doc or in another section") [[#442 report](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/issues/442#issuecomment-6357235012)]. The doc tells the agent to look elsewhere before restoring. These flags are cheap to clear by hand, but they're half of what a run flags at 0.3 (79 of 150 on R).

**Proposal, in order. Stop at the first step that answers it:**
1. **Code only.** For each sentence the pass would send, follow the links in its successor section to the destination doc (at the same tree, as `prove-no-loss.sh` resolves `--docs-dir` / `--also`). If the sentence is `kept` there (the same substring test as today, measured harmless in CR 469), status `delegated`, and nothing is sent. This costs nothing per run. Measure how many of the set's delegated positives it resolves, and that it resolves no true drop.
2. **Only if step 1 leaves a real share unresolved:** a second Noul, "Does `linked_section` state what `sentence` requires or forbids?", with the linked destination section as state. Asked only where the successor links somewhere, so it's one extra call on those sentences.
3. **Decide the default from the numbers.** If `delegated` removes false re-reads and costs no true drop, it becomes default-on with an opt-out flag. Otherwise it stays opt-in, or the issue closes as not planned, with the numbers. Either is a fine outcome for the epic.

**Measuring it:**
- **#442's committed set is the base:** `tests/fixtures/typesafe-eval/tightened-rules/`, 421 sentences from 49 curations in 9 public repos.
- **Labels:** the current label says *yes* for "moved behind a link", because the pass saw only the successor. This child needs a **second label column** on the delegated positives: *held at the destination*, or *not*. Add it beside `labels.tsv`, appending, never re-sampling (#441's lesson).
- **Inputs:** `inputs.jsonl` holds each record's successor but not the link targets' text. Recover the destinations from the same public clones at each curation commit, and re-check visibility at commit time (the fixture README, step 1).
- **Report** the R-slice flag count and catches at 0.3, with and without `delegated`, plus every true drop it would have hidden. **The pass exists for recall:** hiding one real drop costs more than a hundred cleared re-reads.

**Hazards:**
- **A link is a claim, not proof.** A pointer to a doc that doesn't hold the rule is exactly the drop the iron law guards. The substring test is the floor; a looser match needs its own measurement.
- **`prove-no-loss.sh` stays byte-unchanged.** If the pass needs destination paths, extend `--candidates`' records (output only), and prove the identity again on the 66 real curations, as #442 did.
- **Docs:** `references/keep-cut-rubric.md`'s tightened-rules subsection (SKILL.md byte-unchanged).

**Out of scope:** the 0.3 threshold (decided), and subtle weakenings ("must" becoming "is"), which #442 documented as a limit.

child.title: curating-context: a TypeSafe Noul per index line checks it still describes its doc, and flags sibling lines that steal a topic's route
child.body:
**What:** an agent picks a reference doc by its **line in the policy file's index**, and curating-context has measured that being reachable through links doesn't make a doc findable ([cohort-patterns.md § Reachable is not routable](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/curating-context/references/cohort-patterns.md#reachable-is-not-routable)). A doc named nowhere in the policy file fell from 12/12 to 2/12 tasks reaching it, and a sibling line that named a topic better took every first hop. `docs_unindexed` counts docs with **no** line. Nothing checks whether an existing line still **describes** its doc after the doc grew, split, or absorbed a demotion. `check-counts.sh` bounds a line's *length*, not its accuracy.

**Proposal:** an optional, advisory pass in Phase 6.5:
- **Code** pairs each index line with its target doc's headings and opening paragraph, and lists the doc's `##` topics.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per policy file:**
  - a **Noul** per index line: "Would an agent reading only `index_line` expect to find what `doc.headings` covers, with no major topic missing and none claimed that isn't there?"
  - a **Noul** per (doc topic, index line naming a *different* doc): "Does `index_line` claim `topic` more directly than its own doc's line does?" This flags the sibling line that steals a route.
- **Output:** inaccurate lines and topic collisions, ranked, beside `check-seams.sh`'s report.

**Scope:** this checks whether a line *describes its doc accurately*. It does not *simulate routing*. Whether an agent actually finds the doc is a property of the agent's model, and the measurement in cohort-patterns.md should keep using the real agent. Jev standing in for it would measure a different model.

**Must not:** rewrite index lines, or count toward any gated telemetry field.

**Why it matters:** an inaccurate index line is a routing loss that every task pays and no current field records. The curation that caused it, a demotion that grew a doc, is exactly the run in which nobody re-reads that line.

**Evaluation:** index-line rewrites in cohort curation diffs (a line re-worded after its doc changed) are positives. The routing measurements above give a small set with known outcomes.

- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).

child.title: curating-context: a TypeSafe Choice per section as a second reading of the Phase 3 class, recorded in the telemetry row
child.body:
**What:** Phase 3 gives each `##` section (and each subsection over ~5% of the file) one class, A/B/C/D, from [keep-cut-rubric.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/curating-context/references/keep-cut-rubric.md). That class is the most consequential call in a run: the skill itself says "compressing class B is wasted work, deleting class A is damage." Yet it is pure agent judgment, and the ledger records only the actions that followed (`demote:X`, `prune:Y`). Neither the class nor how close the call was is recorded.

**Proposal:** add an optional script that sends the policy file to [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) Jev as structured state (`sections[i].heading`, `.text`, `.tokens`). The request asks:
- one **Choice** per section over A/B/C/D, with each option's criteria taken from the rubric's class definitions, so the classes mean the same thing in the script as in the rubric;
- one **Noul** per section: "Does `sections[i].text` restate a default a capable coding agent already follows?" This is the one class-D clause a model can judge. *Duplicates another part of the surface* and *disproven* stay with Phase 2's scripts.

All of these go in one request ([speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md)). The script outputs JSON: per section, the class, its per-class probabilities, the confidence, and the Noul.

**How it's used:**
1. The agent's class stays authoritative. A section where Jev's class differs, or its confidence is low, gets a second look before Phase 4. It is never re-classed automatically.
2. A new telemetry field (e.g. `class_contested`, the number of contested sections, `null` when the step didn't run) lets the cohort roll-up see which classes are hard to call.

**Must not:** license a delete. The iron law's warrants (relocated, duplicated, disproven) are unchanged. A "D" from Jev with no warrant only means "look here".

**Why it matters:** the class is the one call in the run nobody checks. A probability distribution per section makes a contested call visible, before it turns into an edit, and after it, in the ledger.

**Evaluation:** past cohort runs give a labelled set. The ledger's action tags plus the curation diffs recover which sections were demoted, tightened or pruned. Measure agreement against those first. Cost [estimated]: at the listed $0.042/Mtok input price, a 6k-token policy file plus the questions costs well under a cent per run.

**Constraints shared with the other TypeSafe proposals:**

child.title: coordinating-epics: rank harvest candidates with a TypeSafe Noul per (paragraph, open child), so a note reaches a child it never names
child.body:
**What:** check-in §2, Harvest ([check-in.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/coordinating-epics/references/check-in.md#2-harvest)), reads the closing comment, the PR, and every comment since the hand-off. From them it routes contract diffs, `For #N:` notes, asides in prose, verification debt and corrections to the children they affect. An explicit `For #N:` heading names its target. The hard cases have no heading: a contract diff that should reach "every downstream child", or a later child's precondition mentioned in passing. Here the coordinator has to match a paragraph to a child it never names. Several log entries cite a note that didn't reach its child (archiver 19, 32; private-backlog 103, 110).

**Proposal:** add an optional script that produces a ranked list of harvest candidates:
- Code splits the harvest sources into paragraphs and fetches the open children's titles and bodies through `gh`.
- One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per source comment, with that comment's paragraphs and the open children in the state:
  - a **Noul** per (paragraph, child): "Does `paragraphs[i]` change a fact, contract, or step that `children[j].body` relies on?";
  - a **Choice** per paragraph over the harvest kinds in §2: contract diff, note for a later child, new state/code/message, verification debt, accepted limitation, correction to a claim, answer to a later child's step, or **none**.
- Output: (paragraph, child, kind, probability) rows sorted by the Noul, written to the coordinator's scratch, where it reads them beside `scan.json`.

**Must not:** write to GitHub. The coordinator still verifies each candidate and writes the "Changed since filed" comment, and the "coordinator never writes code" rule is unchanged. The script only reorders what the coordinator reads first.

**Why it matters:** a note that never reaches its child surfaces only when that child's implementer runs into it. The cost of a missed harvest is paid late and in someone else's thread.

**Evaluation:** the process-log issues (#428, #431 and their predecessors) record harvest misses together with the comment and child involved. Replaying those pairs gives a labelled set before the step is enabled anywhere. This is the [re-ranking](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md) pattern; a ranked list doesn't need a threshold to be useful.

child.title: coordinating-epics: a TypeSafe Choice per new item proposes its §3 slot, with a Noul per open child for duplicates
child.body:
**What:** at each check-in, `scan.sh` reports new items through three cursors (number watermark, updated-since, commit range). [check-in.md §3](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/coordinating-epics/references/check-in.md#3-re-scan-and-slot) then classifies each new item as **child**, **closed-in-fact**, **split**, **out of epic**, **duplicate**, or **park**, which is a closed set of six. The coordinator classifies each item by reading it, and a re-scan can return many items at once.

**Proposal:** an optional script that reads `scan.json` and proposes a slot for each item. One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per item, with the item (title, body, labels, state, linked PRs), the epic's goal and child lines, and the open children in the state:
- a **Choice** over the six outcomes, each option's criteria taken from §3's own definitions;
- a **Noul** per open child: "Does `item` describe the same work as `open_children[j]`?" The top match names the duplicate's survivor;
- a **Noul**: "Does `item` contain both work this epic covers and work it does not?" This is a signal for a split.

The output is the proposed slot, its probabilities and confidence, and the top duplicate candidate, written beside `scan.json`. Low confidence means the item gets a full read.

**Must not:** act. *closed-in-fact* still needs §1's evidence (merged, CI green on the final SHA, live), and all edits still go through `epic-edit.sh`, whose refusals are unchanged. A proposal only orders the coordinator's reading.

**Why it matters:** a duplicate or an out-of-epic item that gets slotted as a child costs a whole hand-off. The six outcomes are already defined, which is exactly the shape a Choice needs.

**Shares a loader with #436:** both read the same state (new comments or items, open children). Build them on one fetch.

**Evaluation:** where check-in log lines and epic edit history record how past items were slotted, they form the labelled set. Replay them before enabling the step.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435–#437):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.

- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

child.title: orchestrating-issue-backlog: at each batch boundary, a TypeSafe Noul per (claim, merged hunk) flags issue-body decay before workers launch
child.body:
**What:** orchestrating-issue-backlog carries a **runtime note on issue-body decay** ([SKILL.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/orchestrating-issue-backlog/SKILL.md)): "the backlog is N sequential mutations of what the bodies describe, so re-verify the specifics of any issue whose files an earlier batch touched (Worker step 5); the later the batch, the staler the body." reviewing-architecture records how bad this gets, measured: a 13-issue backlog carved from one review "carried a material error in **every** issue body by implementation time." One finding's branch-point table was 5 of 7 stale, because an earlier batch had changed a column type (process-log 2026-08-09 observo). The re-verify step relies on each worker noticing that its issue's files moved.

**Proposal:** an optional script the coordinator runs at each batch boundary, before workers launch:
- **Code** collects, for each issue in the next batch, the hunks merged since the issue was filed (or since its last "Changed since filed" comment) that touch the paths, symbols or tables its body cites. It also splits the body into claim sentences.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per issue,** a **Noul** per (claim, hunk): "Does `hunks[k]` make `claims[i]` untrue or out of date, for example a line, count, signature, column type or file it states?"
- **Output:** for each issue, the flagged claims with the hunk and merge commit that invalidates them. The worker's brief carries it, and the coordinator posts it as a "Changed since filed" comment, as coordinating-epics does.

**Must not:** edit issue bodies or reorder batches. The worker still re-verifies (step 5), and the script tells it where to look first.

**Why it matters:** the decay concentrates in the later batches, where the work is hardest. A worker that trusts a stale body re-does work or implements against a shape that's gone.

**Shares machinery with #436 and #439:** the same fetch of issues and comments, and the same paragraph and hunk splitting. Build it on that loader.

**Evaluation:** the Step 5 rescope comments and process-log entries record which bodies were stale and why. Replaying their batches gives labelled (claim, hunk) pairs.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).

- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

child.title: orchestrating-issue-backlog: pre-score the Step 4 rubric with TypeSafe Scores, weights stay in the formula
child.body:
**What:** [Step 4](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/orchestrating-issue-backlog/SKILL.md#step-4-scoring-rubric) scores every issue on three dimensions with concrete 1–3 levels, then combines them with a formula the user may re-weight: `(Foundation × 2) + (Correctness × 2) + Scope`. The agent assigns each score by reading.

**Proposal:** an optional script that pre-scores the backlog. This is TypeSafe's [composite-scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) pattern: Jev scores the dimensions, and the weights stay in code.
- **Correctness Risk** and **Scope Clarity:** one **Score** each per issue, with the rubric's level descriptions as the levels, verbatim.
- **"Does this issue name a decision it leaves unresolved?"** One **Noul** per issue. This feeds the existing *decide-then-rescore* rule directly, so the decisions to raise at the approval gate surface before the table is presented.
- **Foundation Leverage** is relational, not a property of one issue. Ask one **Noul** per ordered pair: "Would resolving `issues[i]` unblock or simplify `issues[j]`?" Code then maps the count of confident pairs onto levels 1–3. Pairs grow as n²: for 40 issues that is 1,560 questions. Prefilter pairs in code (shared paths, labels, cross-references) and measure the request sizes against the 64k-per-request / 32k-per-question limits before choosing a batching scheme.

The table shows Jev's scores beside the agent's. A score with low confidence, or one that disagrees with the agent's, marks an issue to read in full.

**Bonus:** when the user re-weights the formula at the gate, the table recomputes without re-running inference, because the judgments haven't changed.

**Must not:** replace the HARD-GATE. The user still approves the scored table, and blast radius stays a sequencing input computed by code.

**Evaluation:** the approved tables in cohort design docs, and the re-scores recorded in process-log entries (e.g. the 14 → 16 move in the 2026-08-11 observo log), are the labels.

child.title: docs conventions: an advisory TypeSafe Choice per added sentence flags a present-tense claim about another repo, without the network gate the convention rejected
child.body:
**What:** [docs/CONVENTIONS.md § Claims about another repository](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/CONVENTIONS.md#claims-about-another-repository) bans stating another repo's current state in the present tense ("every cohort repo runs…"). A claim must be either **a shape without names** or **a dated observation** with the command that re-derives it, and **an event** needs neither form. The rule came from #322: a present-tense claim about `CannObserv/power-map`'s `scripts/pre-ship.sh` was cited as evidence two days after the file was deleted. The convention also says **"Do not gate this"**, because a test that queries GitHub for thirteen repos adds a network dependency to the suite. So today nothing catches a violation except a reviewer's eye.

**Proposal:** the gate the convention rejected would *verify* each claim against GitHub. Spotting the banned form is a different judgment, one that needs no GitHub call: is this sentence about another repo, and which of the convention's forms is it in? An optional, advisory script runs over the **added lines of a diff** in `*.md` files:
- **Code** splits the added prose into sentences, skipping fenced code and inline code spans.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per diff,** a **Choice** per sentence over {**shape without names**, **dated observation**, **event**, **present-tense claim about another repo's current state**, **not about another repo**}. Each option's criteria quote the convention's own definition and examples.
- **Output:** the sentences whose peak is *present-tense claim*, with the convention's two allowed rewrites linked.

**Where it runs:** beside `pre-ship.sh` or in reviewing-code's documentation pass, **never inside the pytest suite**. That keeps the convention's network-dependency reason intact.

**Must not:** block a commit. A flagged sentence is a prompt to choose a form; the author may decide it's an event.

**Why it matters:** the convention is right that verification can't be gated, but detection can be advisory, and a present-tense claim slips through review because it reads as a plain fact.

**Evaluation:** `git log -p` over `docs/` and `skills/**/*.md` finds sentences rewritten from present tense into an observation, which are positives (e.g. the #322 fix). The convention's own examples are fixed test cases.

- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).

child.title: process logs: TypeSafe Nouls spot a finding's second occurrence, the signal the promotion rule waits for
child.body:
**What:** three skills keep a per-run process log: [coordinating-epics](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/coordinating-epics/references/process-log.md), [orchestrating-issue-backlog](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/orchestrating-issue-backlog/references/process-log.md) and [patching-hosts](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/patching-hosts/references/process-log.md). Each promotes a recurring pattern into the skill and lists it under *Rules promoted into the skill* with the findings it came from. coordinating-epics states the rule as "a pattern that recurs in two runs, or that prevented damage once, is promoted." patching-hosts adds where a rule goes: a pattern that recurs on one environment goes into that environment's profile, and one that recurs across environments goes into the core. Spotting the recurrence is done by memory. A new run's findings have to be matched against every earlier entry's findings and every promoted rule, and as the logs grow, a second occurrence can go unnoticed.

**Proposal:** an optional script that runs when an entry is journaled. Code parses the new entry's findings, the promoted rules, and the earlier entries' unpromoted findings. Then one [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per new finding asks:
- a **Noul** per promoted rule: "Is `finding` another instance of `rules[j]`?" A high value means the finding should be cited under that rule, not re-promoted;
- a **Noul** per earlier unpromoted finding: "Do `finding` and `prior[k]` describe the same failure, even in different words or repos?" A high value means a **promotion candidate**: the second occurrence the rule is waiting for;
- a **Choice** over the skill's SKILL.md and reference headings (for patching-hosts, also its `environments/<id>.md` profiles), plus *none*: "Which section owns the step this finding is about?" The answer names where a promoted rule would land.

**Output:** for each finding, any existing-rule matches, promotion candidates with the earlier finding's run and number, and the owning section. All of it goes into the journaling agent's view.

**Must not:** promote anything. Promotion stays a judged edit to SKILL.md, made under the self-budget ratchet.

**Why it matters:** this rule is how a run's lessons reach the skill, and it depends on someone remembering that they've seen a pattern before. Across three skills, many runs and hundreds of numbered findings, that memory is the bottleneck. The section map also turns the logs into data: which sections produce the most lessons is a measured signal for which sections to revise.

**Evaluation:** the *Rules promoted into the skill* lists already record which findings were judged to be the same pattern (e.g. "From 2026-10-09 archiver (10, 17), 2026-10-13 status (18) …"). Those groupings are a ready-made labelled set for the pair Noul.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).

child.title: shipping-work: a TypeSafe Noul per issue requirement builds a requirements-vs-commits table for the Step 6 close gate
child.body:
**What:** every shipping-work variant has the same Step 6 HARD-GATE ([baseline](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/shipping-work/SKILL.md#step-6--close-github-issues)): "Re-read the issue body. Confirm each stated requirement is addressed in commits. If any requirement is missing: do NOT close." The check is a single act of reading, and nothing in what the user sees shows which requirements were matched to which commits.

**Proposal:** an optional script that runs before `close-issue.sh` and produces a requirements table:
- **Code extracts the requirements** from the issue body (checklist items, list items, paragraphs under a "Suggested fix" or "Acceptance" heading) and the evidence from the commit range: messages, changed paths, and the hunks of each changed file.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per issue,** with the requirements and the evidence in the state. It asks a **Noul** per requirement: "Do the changes in `commits` address `requirements[i]` as stated, not just touch the same area?"
- **Output:** a requirement / probability / closest-commit table. The agent shows it at the gate, and a weak row turns into the gate's existing question: descope or continue?

**Must not:** close anything, or count as the gate's verification. The HARD-GATE's wording is unchanged, and a high probability doesn't excuse re-reading the body.

**Why it matters:** an issue closed with a missing requirement is reopened by whoever runs into the gap, usually long after the context is gone. A table makes a requirement that got skimmed past visible at the one moment it is cheap to act on.

- **Context limits:** diffs push against the 64k-per-request / 32k-per-question limits. Send hunks scoped to each requirement's paths, not the whole diff.

**Evaluation:** in this repo, issues closed and later reopened, plus "descoped to #N" comments, give positives. Issues closed and never revisited give negatives.

child.title: reviewing-code: a TypeSafe Score per finding as a calibration check on its severity tier
child.body:
**What:** Phase 3 sorts findings into 🔴 Bugs / 🟡 Issues to fix / 💭 Minor based on the reviewer's judgment alone. Nothing checks a tier call. Yet the tier steers the user's directives, especially a blanket `address the findings`, which answers every tier in one pass.

**Proposal:** after Phase 3.5 verification, an optional script reads each finding (the required `What:` / `Why it matters:` / `Suggested fix:` labels make that parse reliable) plus the diff hunk at its `file:line`, and sends one [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request with:
- a **Score** per finding on three levels, each describing a concrete situation (e.g. *produces wrong output, a crash, or data loss on an input the code can reach* / *a correctness or maintenance cost a user or later change will hit* / *style, naming, or an observation with no failure attached*);
- a **Noul** per finding: "Does `findings[i].why` name a concrete failure, meaning specific inputs or state leading to a specific wrong outcome?"

Where the Score's peak level differs from the reviewer's tier, or its [confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md) is low, the report marks the finding *tier contested*. The user then sees which calls to look at before giving directives. The reviewer's tier stays authoritative, and nothing is re-tiered automatically.

**Why it matters:** a finding that is really a bug, filed under 💭, can be stetted with the rest of its tier. A 🔴 with no failure scenario costs the user a careful read for nothing.

**Prerequisite:** directives aren't recorded durably today. Only fixed findings land, as `CR N` commits, and stet/GH decisions disappear. Recording each finding's tier and directive over a few rounds builds the labelled set; without it there is nothing to measure agreement against.

**Scope:** the variants (`-php`, `-python-fastapi`, `-python-click`) are self-contained, so start in the baseline and copy to the variants only once agreement has been measured.

**Constraints shared with the other TypeSafe proposals:**
- **Opt-in and advisory.** If `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is missing, the step skips and says so loudly, and the run goes on exactly as it does today. The opt-in knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md), which `test_skills_knob_inventory.py` requires.
- **Data leaves the machine.** This sends repo text to typesafe.ai. Today the only API call any skill script makes is `measure-context.sh --exact`'s token count, and that sends no text to be judged. Some cohort repos are private, so the opt-in is per repo, never cohort-wide.
- **Pin the model.** Use `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`. The alias moves when a new version ships, and thresholds tuned against one version don't carry to the next ([models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models.md#aliases)).
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does. A typed answer guarantees the shape of the answer, not that it is true.

child.title: typesafe: evaluation harness — labelled JSONL in, agreement and calibration out
child.body:
Foundation child for the TypeSafe epic (#451). Every proposal in #435–#447 says to **measure before gating**. This gives them one way to measure.

**What:** a repo-level dev tool, `scripts/typesafe-eval.py`, that is not shipped inside any skill:
- **Input:** a labelled JSONL set, one row per case: `id`, `state`, `questions`, `expected` (a choice, a level, or a yes/no), and an optional `source`. It also accepts a cached-responses file, so a re-run replays without calling the API.
- **Output:**
  - for Choice/Score: agreement, a confusion matrix, and accuracy by confidence band;
  - for Noul: precision and recall at a sweep of thresholds, plus a calibration table;
  - in every case: the model ID that answered, and the token usage.
- **Uses SUB1's client.** The evaluator owns no HTTP code.

**Boundary:** a labelled set drawn from a **private** cohort repo is never committed here. It stays in scratch or off-repo, and only its aggregate result is posted on the child's issue. A committed fixture must come from public material (this repo, its issues, or public cohort repos).

**Done when:** the tool is merged with structural tests that run on a fake transport and a cached-responses file, `--help` documents the JSONL schema, and `scripts/pre-ship.sh` is green.
